issues.reason: Sealing under Theme is restricted to the attitude construction — "Only for a finite clausal complement" — and every non-finite eventive complement the instruction set does route (causative "an embedded complement eventuality is reified and attached to the matrix verb by Theme", inceptive, perception) is reified at TOP LEVEL with no status atom, which is the device that leaves occurrence unstated.

This is a gap claim, not a defect claim: the subject of "agreeing to come" is an unexpressed controlled subject with no antecedent and no pronoun, so there is no licensed filler — minting a participant the text never names would itself be the over-assertion (cf. the imperative rule's "mint no addressee referent") — and the reviewer's own notes concede the ellipsis forces it.

gaps_confirmed: verbless expressive speech-act formula ("Thanks", "Sorry", "Congratulations") — nothing says whether it is asserted as an occurring event or how its participants are handled

subject-control infinitival complement ("agree to V", "promise to V") — only causatives, aspectual inceptives, purpose infinitives and degree-governed infinitives are covered, so neither the sealing/reification choice nor controller-copying is stated
gerund clause as the object of a preposition — the oblique rule's "object NP follows the ordinary NP rules" does not cover a clausal object
new_gaps: an ELIDED speech-act participant (the implicit thanker and addressee of a bare "Thanks for …") has no licensed filler at all, so neither the thanking's nor the agreeing's agent can be recorded — the "mint no addressee referent" rule is stated only for imperatives
repair_summary: Unsealed the control complement: added top-level `(: e_come (Member sk_come_1 come) (STV 1.0 0.99))` and changed e_theme to `(Theme sk_agree_1 sk_come_1)`; no tense/status atom on it, so occurrence stays unstated; e_thank, e_agree and e_for unchanged.
notes: `(For sk_thank_1 sk_agree_1)` is correct — the agreeing is the ground of the thanking, which the instruction set routes to the preposition-named oblique rather than Beneficiary. The repair uses only the causative/inceptive complement shape; nothing was invented for the elided participants.
